subject: Using "tximport" in R, and stuck on tx2gene

messages.author: 4e113ea40ba2e533
messages.subject: Using "tximport" in R, and stuck on tx2gene
parts:
Hi all,

I posted this question in the MAD.oxli when I first encountered it yesterday, and think I understand a little more what is missing now but still not sure how to solve it.

I ran a snakefile to align my 3'tag-seq data using Salmon, and in the process of the alignment removed some lines of code. 

Upon performing the count file generation step using tximport in R, I realized I don't have a count file folder - just a quant.sf file for each individual subject sequenced. 

The region highlighted in yellow prompts the error message:
Error in all(file.exists(files)) : invalid 'file' argument
In addition: Warning message:
Unknown or uninitialised column: 'files'. 

And the region highlighted in green is where I think I've made a mistake. I thought the tx2gene file was the location of the annotated transcriptome, and hoped that the fact that my alignment did not generate anything with tx2gene would be OK. 


This is my code, with any changes i've made to fit the code in red, and the original code in blue:

# Install the latest version of DEseq2
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
  install.packages("BiocManager")

# load the library
source("https://bioconductor.org/biocLite.R")

BiocManager::install("TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38.knownGene")

BiocManager::install("tximport")

library(tximport)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)


# read in file names 
files <- read_csv("samples_FXTAS_nonribo.csv")

### read in human counts
#original code
tx2gene <- read_tsv("outputs/tx2gene/dogtx2gene.tsv")
canine <- tximport(files = files$files, type = "salmon", tx2gene = tx2gene)
caninecounts <- canine$counts


#my code to work with human transcriptome
library(TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38.knownGene)
txdb <- TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38.knownGene
k <- keys(txdb, keytype="TXNAME")
tx2gene <- select(txdb, k, "GENEID", "TXNAME")

fxtas <- tximport(files = files$files, type = "salmon", tx2gene = tx2gene)


# change rownames for provenance
colnames(caninecounts) <- files$sample

# write to file
write.csv(caninecounts, "outputs/counts/dog_nonribo_counts.csv", quote = F, row.names = T)



(I'm changing everything labeled canine for my human data)

If more info is needed, I can provide it! Just trying to sort out what I need to fix. Sorry if cross-posting this between MAD ad D-RUG is not encouraged.

messages.author: 4b16035cff9b0f8a
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Using "tximport" in R, and stuck on tx2gene
parts:
The error is telling you that the variable "files" (which is the list of files, in red, which means you removed it?) is missing, and you need it on the line that starts with "fxtas" because you call it in the function. Adding that line back might solve the problem.

If that doesn't work, a sample data file and the full R script would be very helpful so that we can see what's actually going on.


Thanks,
Erica

--
Erica Rettig
Ph.D. Candidate
Graduate Group in Ecology, UC Davis
